title: High Pressure at the Screening

patient.name: Mr Goh Wee Kiat
patient.presenting_complaint: Attending a community eye screening; NCT reading comes back high

history.hpc: Mr Goh attends a community eye screening. He says: 'I come for the free eye screening, they say must check eye pressure.' He has no eye symptoms. On NCT his readings are elevated in both eyes. The OT must perform reliable NCT, repeat to confirm, and flag the high readings appropriately.
history.social_hx: Office-based manager. Non-smoker. Asymptomatic, here for screening.

examination_findings.fundus: Not assessed at screening; optic discs to be assessed by doctor

investigations.nct_screening: NCT performed with correct technique: machine contact parts wiped, glasses/contact lenses removed, patient positioned and informed about the air puff, right eye first. Readings elevated, so repeated to confirm consistency. RE 27 mmHg, LE 25 mmHg — above the normal 10-21 mmHg range.
investigations.family_history: Father had glaucoma — a relevant risk factor to flag.

diagnosis: Elevated IOP on NCT screening (both eyes) in an asymptomatic patient with a family history of glaucoma — a screen-positive result that should be flagged for formal assessment (including GAT and optic disc/field evaluation). The OT competency is reliable NCT and appropriate flagging, not diagnosing glaucoma.

immediate: Perform NCT with correct technique (wipe parts, remove glasses/lenses, inform patient, right eye first)
Repeat the readings to confirm the elevated IOP is consistent, not a one-off artefact
Note the family history of glaucoma as an additional risk factor
Flag the elevated IOP as a screen-positive result for formal assessment (e.g., GAT, doctor review)
Document the readings, technique, and that the result was confirmed on repeat
Reassure the patient and explain the need for further checks without diagnosing
follow_up: Refer for formal IOP measurement (Goldmann), optic disc, and visual field assessment by the clinic/doctor
Advise the patient to attend the recommended follow-up appointment
patient_education: Explain NCT is a quick air-puff test and that his pressure reading is higher than normal
Explain that high pressure alone is not a diagnosis, but it needs further checking, especially with his family history
Encourage him to attend the follow-up assessment
Reassure him that he has no symptoms now and this is exactly why screening is useful

key_points: Confirms the screening context and absence of symptoms
Elicits the family history of glaucoma as a risk factor
Confirms no contraindication and that glasses/lenses are removed
Explains the air-puff test to the patient
Performs NCT with correct hygiene, positioning, and right-eye-first technique
Repeats readings to confirm the elevated IOP is consistent
Records the readings against the normal range (10-21 mmHg)
Recognises the elevated IOP as a screen-positive result needing further assessment
Considers the family history as raising glaucoma risk
Understands NCT alone does not diagnose glaucoma
Knows formal GAT/disc/field assessment is required
Flags the result and refers for formal assessment appropriately
Documents the readings and screening outcome clearly
Explains the result to the patient without over-stating it
